description:
The Promotion of Tiatr Related Activities scheme was launched by the Government of Goa in 2017. 

This initiative aims to support and promote the traditional art form of Tiatr, which is a popular theatrical performance in the Konkani language. 

Tiatr has a rich cultural heritage in Goa and is a significant aspect of the state's identity. 

The scheme was introduced to provide financial assistance to artists and organizations involved in Tiatr productions. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to encourage the growth and sustainability of Tiatr as an art form. 

The government aims to enhance the quality of Tiatr performances and ensure that they reach a wider audience. 

One of the measurable targets of the scheme is to increase the number of Tiatr performances across Goa by 20% annually. 

The scheme also aims to provide training and workshops for aspiring Tiatr artists. 

This includes initiatives to improve their skills in acting, scriptwriting, and stage management. 

The financial benefits under this scheme include grants for organizing Tiatr shows. 

Eligible organizations can receive up to ₹2 lakh for each Tiatr production. 

Individual artists can also apply for financial support of up to ₹50,000 for their performances. 

The scheme is designed to cover various aspects of Tiatr productions, including set design, costumes, and marketing. 

Eligibility for this scheme is primarily focused on individuals and organizations involved in Tiatr. 

Organizations must be registered under the Societies Registration Act of 1860. 

Individual artists must have a minimum of three years of experience in Tiatr performances. 

There is no specific age limit for applicants, but they must demonstrate a commitment to the art form. 

The application process involves several steps to ensure transparency and accountability. 

Interested parties must submit a detailed proposal outlining their planned Tiatr production. 

This proposal should include information about the cast, crew, and budget estimates. 

Applicants must also provide proof of their registration as an organization or their experience as an individual artist. 

The required documents include a copy of the registration certificate, identity proof, and a detailed project report. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by a committee formed by the Department of Art and Culture, Government of Goa. 

The committee evaluates the proposals based on their artistic merit and feasibility. 

Successful applicants are notified within 30 days of submission. 

Disbursement of funds occurs in two installments. 

The first installment of 50% is released upon approval of the project. 

The second installment is released after the successful completion of the Tiatr production. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Art and Culture, Government of Goa. 

For any inquiries or assistance, applicants can contact the department at their office located in Panaji, Goa. 

The contact number for the Department of Art and Culture is +91 832 222 5111. 

The scheme has seen a positive response since its inception. 

Many Tiatr artists have benefited from the financial support provided. 

This has led to an increase in the number of Tiatr performances in Goa. 

The scheme has also contributed to the preservation of the Konkani language and culture. 

In 2022, it was reported that over 100 Tiatr productions received financial assistance under this scheme. 

This has encouraged younger generations to engage with Tiatr and learn about its significance. 

The government has also organized annual Tiatr festivals to showcase the works of supported artists. 

These festivals provide a platform for artists to present their work to a larger audience. 

The Promotion of Tiatr Related Activities scheme is part of a broader initiative to promote cultural heritage in Goa. 

The government recognizes the importance of traditional art forms in fostering community identity. 

As part of the scheme, workshops are conducted regularly to train new artists. 

These workshops cover various aspects of Tiatr, including music, dance, and scriptwriting. 

The scheme has also facilitated collaborations between experienced artists and newcomers. 

This mentorship approach has proven effective in nurturing talent within the Tiatr community. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹1 crore annually for this scheme. 

This funding is intended to support various activities related to Tiatr. 

The scheme also aims to promote Tiatr beyond Goa, encouraging performances in other states. 

The outreach efforts include organizing shows in neighboring states to attract a wider audience. 

The government has partnered with local cultural organizations to facilitate these performances. 

The Promotion of Tiatr Related Activities scheme reflects the government's commitment to preserving and promoting Goa's cultural heritage. 

It serves as a vital support system for artists and organizations dedicated to Tiatr. 

Through this initiative, the government aims to ensure that Tiatr continues to thrive for future generations. 

The scheme has become a cornerstone of cultural policy in Goa. 

It highlights the importance of traditional art forms in the state's socio-cultural landscape. 

Overall, the Promotion of Tiatr Related Activities scheme is a comprehensive initiative. 

It addresses various aspects of Tiatr production and artist support. 

This makes it a significant step towards preserving Goa's rich artistic traditions. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's recognition of the value of cultural heritage. 

It provides a structured framework for the growth and sustainability of Tiatr. 

The ongoing support from the government has revitalized interest in this traditional art form. 

As a result, Tiatr continues to be a vibrant and dynamic part of Goan culture. 

The scheme is expected to evolve further to meet the changing needs of the Tiatr community. 

Future enhancements may include digital platforms for performances and wider promotional activities. 

This would ensure that Tiatr remains relevant in the modern cultural landscape. 

The Promotion of Tiatr Related Activities scheme is an exemplary model of government support for the arts. 

It showcases how targeted assistance can lead to cultural enrichment and community engagement.
